Direct Stanford Stacks retrieval produced a 55-page PDF; the title page, abstract, empirical-bootstrap sections, Cox resampling-unit passage, and jackknife section were inspected.

alternatives.argument: The item explicitly defines P_n(A)=n^{-1} sum_i 1{z_i in A} and its Dirac-measure form. A separate local proof establishes probability-measure well-definedness from countable additivity of each Dirac measure.

The algorithm explicitly samples n independent uniform indices from the observed n units. The dependent local theorem constructs the finite index law and proves that the resulting records are conditionally IID from P_n.
The definition specifies the complete record attached to a declared atomic unit, defines the unit-compatibility condition, and explicitly makes no validity claim.

The algorithm enumerates every d-subset, evaluates the declared statistic on each complement, and returns the explicitly normalized uniform average. A local finite-subset lemma proves the index family and uniform law are well-defined.

sources.title: B. Efron and R. Tibshirani, The Bootstrap Method for Assessing Statistical Accuracy, Stanford LCS Technical Report 19 / BIO 101 (October 1985)
sources.locator: Stanford LCS report §§1–3, printed pp. 1–16; §10, printed pp. 45–49

contents.name: §1 empirical distribution placing equal mass on the observed values
§2 size-n bootstrap draws from the empirical distribution with replacement
§2 parametric bootstrap from a fitted normal model
contents.reason: This pair defines the empirical nonparametric bootstrap; a fitted parametric resampling model needs its own model and parameter-estimation contract, which is outside the approved BCS-47 scope.

contents.name: §3 complete data triples used as the resampling unit in the Cox example
§10 jackknife standard-error scaling and its linearization relation to the bootstrap
contents.reason: The approved BCS-47 contract defines replicates and their uniform average only; jackknife variance scaling and first-order validity are separate claims assigned to the downstream IID-bootstrap and jackknife pair.

sources.title: P.J. Bickel, F. Götze and W.R. van Zwet, Resampling Fewer Than n Observations: Gains, Losses, and Remedies for Losses, Statistica Sinica 7 (1997)
sources.locator: §3, printed pp. 8–12 (Theorem 3 ends on p. 12; §4 begins on that page)

contents.name: §3 m/n bootstrap with replacement definition
contents.reason: The approved BCS-47 algorithm uses size n; the distinct m-out-of-n replacement scheme and its rate regime are assigned to the later bootstrap-failure and subsampling pair.

contents.name: §3 binomial n-choose-m bootstrap by uniform subsets without replacement
§3 sample-splitting estimator from disjoint blocks
contents.reason: The source identifies sample splitting with a k-fold partition; its resampling and risk target belong to the planned cross-validation pair, not the BCS-47 subset algorithm.

contents.name: §3 Theorem 1 first-order property of the without-replacement m-out-of-n scheme
contents.reason: Theorem 1 is a validity result with m tending to infinity and m/n tending to zero; BCS-47 deliberately proves only the finite subset law and assigns validity regimes to BCS-49.

contents.name: §3 Theorem 2 first-order property of the with-replacement m-out-of-n scheme
contents.reason: Theorem 2 requires the source's asymptotic and stability premises; the BCS-47 scope is algorithm definition and finite-law well-definedness, with m-out-of-n validity assigned to BCS-49.

contents.name: §3 parametric m-out-of-n bootstrap bound under regular-model assumptions
contents.reason: This branch uses a specified parametric model, an estimator, and Hellinger-distance control; it is not a sampling-unit definition or an empirical-law resampling algorithm in BCS-47.

sources.title: Philip B. Stark, Statistics 240 Lecture Notes, Part 8: Resampling Methods (revised 23 April 2008)

contents.name: §1.1 bootstrap as IID sampling from the empirical distribution
§1.2 leave-one-out jackknife replicates and their average

contents.reason: The notes' bias and variance corrections add target-specific scaling to delete-one replicates; BCS-47 keeps those scalings separate and BCS-48 owns the smooth-statistic jackknife analysis.
